construct.diagnosis_or_process: Episodic ataxia type 2 due to CACNA1A dysfunction
construct.mechanism: CACNA1A encodes the alpha-1A subunit of the presynaptic CaV2.1 P/Q-type voltage-gated calcium channel. EA2 commonly results from loss-of-function variants that disturb cerebellar neurotransmission, causing hours-long attacks of ataxia/vertigo with interictal nystagmus and often response to acetazolamide.

construct.primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts

second_answer_attack.strongest_alternative: Episodic ataxia type 1 from KCNA1/Kv1.1 dysfunction.
second_answer_attack.resolution: EA1 typically causes much briefer attacks and interictal myokymia. Hours-long attacks, interictal nystagmus, autosomal-dominant inheritance, and acetazolamide response favor CACNA1A/P-Q-type calcium-channel EA2.
